callout.title: Pre-Mandate Kill Switch
callout.body: Run these four checks before signing an engagement letter; failing any one of them is exactly how the practitioners above lost fees, paid defense bills, or faced buy-backs.
items: Confirm the target is a private company and not a public or shell company before signing the mandate [ALC Lawcast: Finance in Focus — R0kgCi34_1s @ 00:01:37].
Route all deal money through a third-party escrow and never take custody of funds in a securities deal [International Business Brokers Association — 7mV4t9a4PvE @ 00:21:44].
Map every state where a buyer or seller is located, because each of those states may have jurisdiction over the deal [International Business Brokers Association — 7mV4t9a4PvE @ 00:33:49].

If securities change hands, obtain written control assurances before closing and deliver year-end financials plus a balance sheet no more than 120 days old [ALC Lawcast: Finance in Focus — uqd9CdrsWKo @ 00:02:09].

chapters.pull_quote: "However broadly you can imagine it, go broader." — Marlon Paz, Mayer Brown (aG2Bnsxt8Cg @ 00:13:00).
action_checklist: Check whether each deal state has adopted an M&A broker exemption by rule, order, or law before marketing the business there [International Business Brokers Association — 7mV4t9a4PvE @ 00:07:13].
Write the buyer-control reasonable belief into the engagement letter so it is documented from day one [International Business Brokers Association — 7mV4t9a4PvE @ 00:21:04].
Get written disclosure and consent from both parties before taking on any joint representation [ALC Lawcast: Finance in Focus — o-XOblDUBuI @ 00:01:39].
Screen Florida deals against the prior-fiscal-year EBITDA under $25M or gross revenue of $250M ceiling and the 20% control presumption [ALC Lawcast: Finance in Focus — rl3PWicoIaE @ 00:02:43].
Limit advertising to the business location and price range when relying on the M&A broker exemption [ALC Lawcast: Finance in Focus — R0kgCi34_1s @ 00:03:05].

For foreign-firm activity with US persons, sign a chaperone agreement with a US broker-dealer that issues confirms and statements and supervises under FINRA 3110 [Mayer Brown — aG2Bnsxt8Cg @ 00:21:09].

chapters.question_prompt: Which licensing questions and supervisory controls must I examine for business brokerage, real estate brokerage, loan brokerage, or a securities broker-dealer?
chapters.title: Licensing, Supervision, and Brokerage Controls
chapters.subtitle: State-specific licensing discussions, referral fees and commissions, California broker responsibilities, FINRA updates, branch registration, customer reserves, written supervisory procedures, and recordkeeping
chapters.executive_summary: Business Broker Crowd Call operators agree that 17 states require a real estate license to sell a business, with Nevada adding a business broker permit and Illinois demanding securities registration; unlicensed operators face disgorged fees, rescinded deals, and unpaid commissions. In non-licensed states like Texas, Virginia, Maryland and DC, brokers sell personal property freely but stop at the LOI, stay out of lease assignments, and hand real estate to a licensed agent. Street numbers: 10-15% commissions with a $20,000 minimum, a Lehman-style ladder from 10% down to 6%, Rule 1017 triggered at 25% ownership change, OSJs inspected annually versus three-year branch cycles, and six-year and three-year record buckets with two years easily accessible. Disagreement centers on whether a non-required Texas license lets a broker fill purchase agreements, and how far consultant status protects unlicensed operators.

sections.title: 1. The Practitioner Consensus: The 17-State Map, the LOI Ceiling, and Unlicensed Exposure
paragraphs: Every Business Broker Crowd Call operator works from the same map: 17 states require a license to sell a business, including Washington, Oregon, California, Utah, Florida, Arizona and Colorado, while Texas does not [Wj1uuYyuyQk @ 00:01:03] [22hjuZT2usA @ 00:00:26]. The trigger is where the target business sits, not where the brokerage is incorporated, so a Delaware-based shop pulling national leads checks each listing's state first. The tool is unglamorous: search which states require a real estate license, print the Business Brokerage Press list, pin it to the wall, and check it on every inbound call. Two states break the pattern. Nevada stacks a business broker permit on top of the real estate license, and Illinois swaps the license for registration with the state Securities Commission, which is why one speaker corrects the count to 16 plus Illinois [uRVS3zWAYwI @ 00:00:47]. California splits the tiers: a broker license runs independently, while a salesperson license must hang under a broker. In Florida, Joe Shemansky, chairman of the Business Brokers of Florida, states that under Florida Real Estate Law 475 anyone transacting a business sale on behalf of another needs a valid DBPR license, checkable through the verify-a-license button at myfloridalicense.com [JkYDV-Gr_qE @ 00:00:06].

The second point of agreement is that unlicensed brokering is free until it is not. A Business Broker Crowd Call speaker compares it to doing 85 in a 65: nobody cares until a lawsuit drags you into a courtroom, where opposing attorneys lead with the missing license [22hjuZT2usA @ 00:01:55]. Depending on state law, deals can be unwound and rescinded, fees disgorged, and the unlicensed party left on the hook for damages to the other side; in California the speaker has watched a seller's attorney tell an unlicensed operator who ran the entire transaction that they were not getting paid, and to sue if they disliked it [22hjuZT2usA @ 00:03:13]. Enforcement from the field runs through complaints: a buyer or seller files with the Department of Real Estate, which issues a cease and desist, though the speaker expects most offenders keep operating. Joe Shemansky pushes the same lever, urging Florida buyers and sellers to report all unlicensed activity [JkYDV-Gr_qE @ 00:01:52]. Janis Benstock adds the licensed-side risk: a well-known agent was fined $5,000 by the real estate commission for violating billboard advertising guidelines, likely by accident, which is the cost of letting the law go stale after pre-licensure [F2USouPuthI @ 00:01:18].

Operators also agree on where the line sits in non-licensed states. A business is personal property and can be sold all day long without a license; real property is the land, and the moment the seller also wants the building sold, a licensed agent in that state has to carry that piece [CoD81HjwtQo @ 00:00:47]. The same speaker uses a strip mall to size the opportunity: twelve businesses inside, from a flower shop to an auto repair, are all business-broker inventory, but the mall itself is real estate agent work. In Virginia, Maryland and DC, which one operator says require no license for business sales, an unlicensed broker still cannot touch the lease assignment; buyer and seller, a commercial or residential agent, or a closing attorney handles it [Py7d57O-Rxs @ 00:02:04]. Paperwork has the same ceiling. Licensed-state brokers fill in the blanks on purchase agreements, while non-licensed-state brokers stop at the non-binding LOI or risk being accused of practicing law without a license, handing the purchase agreement to an attorney [paYxIXgYO0I @ 00:01:36]. A newer operator flagged the corollary: a deal bundling land, like a gas station owner who owns the dirt, needs a real estate license even in a non-licensed state [Wj1uuYyuyQk @ 00:05:01].

sections.title: 2. Exact Street Mechanics, Tools & Numbers
paragraphs: On fees, the Business Broker Crowd Call standard is 10 to 15% of the deal, written as a percentage with a minimum fee: a contract at 12% with a $20,000 floor turns a $100,000 sale into an effective 20% commission [_4qKlVp4-8s @ 00:00:25]. Above $3 million to $10 million the percentage drops, and the speaker lays out a Lehman-style ladder: 10% on the first million, 9% on the second, 8% on the third, 7% on the fourth, and 6% on everything after, all negotiable, against the 2 to 6% range the questioner cited for commercial transactions [_4qKlVp4-8s @ 00:01:31]. Referral money depends on the sender, not just the broker's license. In California a business broker can pay a referral fee to an unlicensed grocery-store worker who sends a seller, but CPAs cannot take referral fees from non-CPAs and attorneys cannot take them from non-attorneys under the Business and Professions Code [uRVS3zWAYwI @ 00:02:10]. Inside eXp, the mechanics are structural: business sales run through eXp Commercial with a business broker addendum to the independent contractor agreement, because eXp Realty's E&O does not cover business sales while eXp Commercial's does [Py7d57O-Rxs @ 00:02:57].

On the securities side, The Finance Lab walks the broker-dealer build in sequence. Form BD goes through the CRD, and the SEC has 45 days to grant registration or start denial proceedings; FINRA membership is a separate application that checks capital, supervisory procedures and the business plan, SIPC membership is automatic unless the firm sells only mutual funds and variable annuities, and states still need their own registrations [dKOzaPUjfHM @ 00:05:41]. The branch exclusions run on hard counts: a non-primary residence used fewer than 30 business days a year stays a non-branch, a mostly insurance storefront can do 25 securities transactions a year, and trade 26 makes it a branch [dKOzaPUjfHM @ 00:08:27]. Rule 1017 fires at 25% of assets or control; ownership changes file at least 30 days ahead and may close before review ends, while new business lines like a market-making desk must wait for approval. Form BDW takes effect 60 days after filing, and FINRA keeps jurisdiction for two years [dKOzaPUjfHM @ 00:09:44]. CertFuel adds the WSP spec: every review names who is responsible, what is reviewed, how often, and how it is documented, and a principal must hold the registration matching the business line supervised [WYhf4z4Djwk @ 00:01:59].

The money-control mechanics come from the FINOP desk. The FINOP Controller formula sums customer credits plus penalty items, subtracts customer debits after a 1 to 3% charge, and deposits any net credit into the special bank account, usually with a cushion above the calculated number [-3SAUcV8ljM @ 00:02:06]. Controls are specific: two or more finance or operations staff prepare and review, source data is imported straight into the Excel workbook to cut manual input, each line item carries a threshold that forces extra analysis, finance, operations and treasury meet before deposit instructions go out, and finance keeps timestamps, approvals and bank confirms after treasury executes [-3SAUcV8ljM @ 00:07:26]. FINRA's Sarah Kanny flags that firms averaging more than $500 million in reserve-formula credits over the last 12 month-end FOCUS reports moved from weekly to daily computation as of June 30, 2026 [BV647oU5rB0 @ 00:02:34]. Records follow VoraPrep's buckets: foundational documents like articles of incorporation for life, blotters, ledgers and customer account records for six years, correspondence, ads, WSPs and U4/U5 for three years, the first two years of both shorter buckets easily accessible, and everything electronic stored in WORM format, write once, read many [Dw1n0a_kMu0 @ 00:05:46].

callout.title: How Operators Stay Paid and Stay Clean Across State Lines
callout.body: Field moves the speakers use to close deals outside their home turf and keep capital and licensing exposure under control.
items: In a non-licensed state, act as if you are transacting under your home state's license rules, so any dispute shows you followed a known regulatory standard instead of a free-for-all [Business Broker Crowd Call — _4qKlVp4-8s @ 00:02:06].

When a listing lands in a licensed state where you hold nothing, partner with a local licensee whose name and license number go on all the paperwork while you work in the background [Business Broker Crowd Call — Wj1uuYyuyQk @ 00:01:41].

eXp agents doing out-of-state deals call their own state broker first; that broker checks a chart showing whether the target state permits it and whether a form must go to that state's designated broker [Business Broker Crowd Call — CoD81HjwtQo @ 00:06:41].

M&A firms paid in restricted shares can treat them as allowable assets up to the liability owed to a registered person if the shares sit in the firm's name at fair value, the written agreement pays only in shares, and the rep acknowledges general creditor risk [Public Company Accounting Oversight Board - PCAOB — BV647oU5rB0 @ 00:43:33].

sop_steps.title: Screen the Deal Location
sop_steps.action: Check the business's state against the printed 17-state list before quoting a fee.
sop_steps.detail: If the state is not on the list, verify anyway: one operator gets a legal opinion from a real estate or business lawyer in a state like North Dakota before transacting there [Business Broker Crowd Call — CoD81HjwtQo @ 00:05:13].

sop_steps.title: Split Real Property From Personal Property
sop_steps.action: Separate the business assets from any land, building, or lease in the deal.
sop_steps.detail: Sell the business yourself, but hand land sales and lease assignments to a state-licensed agent, the parties, or a closing attorney unless you hold a license in that state [Business Broker Crowd Call — Py7d57O-Rxs @ 00:02:04].

sop_steps.title: Price the Engagement
sop_steps.action: Write a percentage fee with a minimum, then ladder it down on larger deals.
sop_steps.detail: Use a structure like 12% with a $20,000 minimum on Main Street deals and a 10%-9%-8%-7%-6% ladder by the million on bigger transactions, all negotiable [Business Broker Crowd Call — _4qKlVp4-8s @ 00:00:47].

sop_steps.title: Paper the Deal to the Right Ceiling
sop_steps.action: Fill purchase agreements only where the state license covers it; otherwise stop at the LOI.
sop_steps.detail: In licensed states like California, brokers fill in the blanks on purchase agreements; in Texas or Montana, stop at the LOI and let an attorney draft or review the purchase agreement [Business Broker Crowd Call — paYxIXgYO0I @ 00:01:00].

sections.heading: Where Practitioners Disagree & Alternative Playbooks
paragraphs: The sharpest split is how much freedom a broker really has outside the 17 license states. One Business Broker Crowd Call host calls non-license states completely unregulated and says the broker there is really just acting as a business consultant who can do whatever they want. In the same breath the host hedges the play: the safest bet is to run every deal as if it sat in your home state and follow your own license rules, so if anything blows up you can show you followed every regulation you already live under [_4qKlVp4-8s @ 00:02:06]. Inside license states the consultant label gets no respect. A dental-practice broker asking about Washington reports a rival insisting a consultant title dodges the real estate license, and the host fires back that it is not a problem until it is, like doing 85 in a 65 until a cop lights you up, because the opposing attorney leads with the missing license the moment a lawsuit starts [22hjuZT2usA @ 00:01:35] [22hjuZT2usA @ 00:01:55]. Florida takes the hardest line: Joe Shemansky, chairman of the Business Brokers of Florida, states that anyone transacting a business sale on behalf of another must hold a valid DBPR real estate license under Florida law 475 [JkYDV-Gr_qE @ 00:00:06].

The second fork is footprint. The same Crowd Call host refuses the 50-state route outright: licensing in every state, then chasing continuing ed and renewing every so many years, would be a nightmare and a full-time job in and of itself, and the host says they would never even consider it [CoD81HjwtQo @ 00:04:15]. When a lead lands in a license state, the alternative playbook is to either get licensed there or partner with a local licensee, work the deal in the background, and put that partner's name and license number on all of the paperwork [Wj1uuYyuyQk @ 00:02:00]. Ian Tucker, who brokers hard-money and DSCR loans, accepts the opposite outcome on the financing side. Because there is no federal oversight of investment real estate loan brokers, each state writes its own rules, and Tucker warns that anyone operating across the country could end up holding a lot of licenses and registrations across multiple states just to stay compliant as a business owner [VF-_WZaM0iI @ 00:01:13] [VF-_WZaM0iI @ 00:03:24]. So the real disagreement is cost tolerance: the business broker routes around the license map with a licensed partner whose name carries the paperwork, while the loan broker treats a growing stack of state licenses and registrations as the standing price of running a national book of investor loans.

The third fight is over paperwork authority and training. A caller pressed the point that a Texas real estate license should let a broker fill in a business purchase agreement the way California brokers do. The host answered no: selling a business in Texas is not licensed activity, so the license does not reach those contracts any more than it authorizes drafting an employment or consulting agreement for somebody [paYxIXgYO0I @ 00:04:09]. In California, the host adds, the state exam has nothing whatsoever on business brokering, not even one question and no continuing ed on it, so the standing advice to anyone selling businesses there is to join CAB for California-specific education on how business sales actually work [paYxIXgYO0I @ 00:05:57]. Janis Benstock, a Philadelphia broker and instructor, hits the same gap from the residential side and answers it with depth instead of association membership. CE is only 14 hours every two years, which is not enough, and the 240-hour Pennsylvania broker curriculum is worth taking even with no plan to open a brokerage, because it keeps agents out of trouble and unlocks creative structures like options, seller financing, and title workarounds that rescue deals that look dead [F2USouPuthI @ 00:02:29] [F2USouPuthI @ 00:03:20].

sections.heading: Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: The most expensive failure is getting caught unlicensed after doing all the work. A Crowd Call host explains that, depending on state law, transactions can be unwound and rescinded just because the alleged broker was not licensed properly, leaving that person responsible for the commissions received plus damages to the other parties [22hjuZT2usA @ 00:02:33]. The host has watched California deals where the broker, or the person acting as one, handled the entire transaction and the seller's attorney simply refused to pay at the end: you are not licensed properly, we are not paying your fee, and if you don't like it, try to sue us [22hjuZT2usA @ 00:03:33]. Licensed practitioners get burned too. Janis Benstock cites a well-known agent fined $5,000 for not complying with advertising guidelines on a billboard [F2USouPuthI @ 00:01:18]. Benstock adds that the violation probably happened by accident, and admits that after roughly 15 years in real estate they only realized how much law they had forgotten once they started teaching it every day [F2USouPuthI @ 00:01:37]. That is the real trap for producers: these violations are usually accidents, which is exactly why fluency in the rules, not good intent, is what keeps the fine, the clawback, and the refused fee off the books.

The next traps hide inside deal structure, not licensing headlines. In non-license jurisdictions like Virginia, Maryland, and DC, a broker can sell the business but can only go as far as the LOI, because putting together a purchase contract counts as practicing law, and cannot touch the lease assignment without a Virginia real estate license; buyer and seller, a commercial or residential agent, or a closing attorney has to handle it [Py7d57O-Rxs @ 00:02:04]. Real property flips the rules in the other direction. A newer broker found a lead in a non-license state that included real estate, and the host confirmed that a gas station sold together with the land it sits on needs a real estate license even where business sales are unregulated [Wj1uuYyuyQk @ 00:06:04]. The same logic covers the strip mall: the shops inside can be sold by a business broker, but the building itself has to be sold by a real estate agent [CoD81HjwtQo @ 00:03:18]. Coverage is a separate failure point that has nothing to do with state law. At eXp, the realty side's errors and omissions insurance does not cover business sales; only eXp Commercial's E&O does, and only with a business broker addendum to the independent contractor agreement [Py7d57O-Rxs @ 00:03:17].

Economics checks cut across both worlds. On small Main Street deals, a contract written at 12% with a $20,000 minimum fee turns into a 20% commission on a $100,000 sale [_4qKlVp4-8s @ 00:00:47]. Run that number before signing, because on the smallest listings the minimum, not the percentage, sets the fee the seller will fight. On the broker-dealer side, FINRA's Mark Ramler flags a quiet net capital drain for M&A shops paid in restricted shares: when a portion is owed to a registered person who does not want delivery of illiquid stock, the firm ends up carrying the shares as a non-allowable asset and accruing compensation expense, cutting net worth and net capital unless a written shares-only agreement qualifies it for the new relief [BV647oU5rB0 @ 00:43:09]. The FINOP Controller stresses reconciling cash suspense accounts daily, researching credit items as quickly as possible, and reporting large credit balances up the line before they are resolved, especially for firms running daily reserve calculations [-3SAUcV8ljM @ 00:09:03]. VoraPrep closes the loop on records: six-year and three-year records must sit somewhere easily accessible for the first two years, and a third-party storage facility that takes three days to ship a box does not qualify [Dw1n0a_kMu0 @ 00:04:35].

callout.title: Clear These Four Checks Before Taking the Listing or Opening the Office
callout.body: Every item below comes from a trap a practitioner hit or watched someone else hit; run all four before money, paperwork, or a new location goes live.
items: Check the business location against the license-state list first, then flag the outliers: Nevada requires a business broker permit on top of the real estate license, and Illinois requires registration with the state securities commission [Business Broker Crowd Call — Wj1uuYyuyQk @ 00:02:38].
In a non-license state, stop at the non-binding LOI and stay out of the lease assignment unless you hold a real estate license in that state [Business Broker Crowd Call — Py7d57O-Rxs @ 00:02:21].
Never let a branch manager give final approval on new accounts unless you are ready to run that office as an OSJ with mandatory annual inspections [The Finance Lab — dKOzaPUjfHM @ 00:07:12].

Reconcile cash suspense accounts daily and push large credit balances up the line before they are resolved, especially if the firm runs daily reserve calculations [FINOP Controller — -3SAUcV8ljM @ 00:09:03].

chapters.pull_quote: Registration doesn't magically make a firm honest. What it does is make a firm accountable. It gives regulators handles to pull. — The Finance Lab (dKOzaPUjfHM @ 00:01:00).
action_checklist: Print the business brokerage press list of states that require a real estate license, pin it on the wall, and check it every time a lead calls with a business in a new state [Business Broker Crowd Call — 22hjuZT2usA @ 00:01:05].

For any state you are unsure of, such as North Dakota, pull a legal opinion from a real estate or business attorney in that state before you transact [Business Broker Crowd Call — CoD81HjwtQo @ 00:05:34].
In Florida, verify any broker on the other side of the deal through the DBPR verify a license button at myfloridalicense.com [We Sell Construction Businesses — JkYDV-Gr_qE @ 00:00:50].

Write listing contracts as a percentage with a minimum fee, such as 12% with a $20,000 minimum, and use a modern Lehman scale once deals climb into the millions [Business Broker Crowd Call — _4qKlVp4-8s @ 00:00:47].
Build WSPs that spell out who reviews, what they review, how often, and how the review is documented, and update them promptly whenever the business changes [CertFuel — WYhf4z4Djwk @ 00:01:59].
Store required electronic records in a WORM system and keep six-year and three-year records easily accessible on site for the first two years [VoraPrep — Dw1n0a_kMu0 @ 00:06:04].

chapters.question_prompt: How do I distinguish confidentiality from non-circumvention protection, evaluate agreement templates, and recognize clauses that deserve scrutiny before signing?
chapters.title: NDAs and Non-Circumvention Agreements
chapters.subtitle: NDA and NCND distinctions, commodity-trading commission protection, disputed ICC templates, confidentiality walkthroughs, notarization questions, non-solicitation, non-compete provisions, and signing risks
chapters.executive_summary: Brokers, commodity intermediaries, and CRE listing agents converge on one point: an NDA only stops talking, while a non-circumvention clause stops the deal from closing without you. Practitioners demand identified and authorized signatories, a specific defined opportunity, substantive non-public information, execution before disclosure, and a reasonable term, commonly two to five years with two treated as the safe default. The ICC model occasional intermediary contract, publication 769, is the only genuine ICC NCNDA; any paper quoting ICC 400, 500, or 600 regulations is flagged as fake. Street mechanics include auto-populated DocuSign NDAs that unlock data rooms, liquidated damages clauses, and arbitration chosen deliberately by seat. Disagreements center on arbitration (plaintiff-friendly versus defendant-risky), term length, whether to leave governing law blank, and whether buyers should accept commission-liability language in broker NDAs.

sections.heading: Section 1: The Practitioner Consensus
paragraphs: The first thing every operator in this space hammers is that an NDA and a non-circumvention promise are two different weapons. Attorney Nancy Greene frames the NDA as a 'don't tell anyone about my stuff' clause and names the loophole bluntly: if the other side tells no one and simply uses your opportunity without you, the NDA probably has not been violated, because they just cut you out of the deal. Her fix is a non-circumvention provision, a 'don't do my stuff without me' clause, which she calls possibly the most powerful contract term operators are not using [FOUV15TeRLY @ 00:01:39]. IXH Trading Academy opens with the exact nightmare: a broker introduces a supplier to a buyer, and three weeks later the two close directly with no call, no commission, no credit [5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:00:01]. Their definition stacks two promises into one contract: nobody goes around the introducer without written permission and fee sharing, and prices, client names, shipping data, and terms stay confidential [5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:00:42]. Dr. Chad Michael Altieri puts the asset plainly: in commission, commodity, financing, and cross-border deals, the real asset is not the paper but the access [sm21N5L0nl8 @ 00:00:43]. That gap is why the combined NCNDA exists.

Enforceability prerequisites line up across camps. Trade Base Hub says courts do not enforce agreements where parties cannot be clearly identified, so each party should complete a client information sheet or KYC process and provide valid government-issued photo ID [yrJW_zsMUXM @ 00:00:33]. The same desk names vague scope as one of the most common reasons NCNDAs fail, and insists on a defined opportunity or a formal annexure of scopes updated and executed by all parties. IXH backs the identity layer: list full legal names, representatives, and official addresses, then confirm the signatory holds a power of attorney or right of signature for the company [5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:02:03]. iTopixs, walking a three-party Russian export blend crude NCND, points to the authority warranty in which each party represents it has actual authority and has taken every step required, including a board resolution if needed, and notes the companies sign, not the individuals [l9rVUJ2duT8 @ 00:18:43]. On substance, Trade Base Hub says only substantive and unique information qualifies, while publicly available material is not protected. Timing is non-negotiable too: the NCNDA must be executed before any protected information is shared, signed by authorized parties, and stored with proper records [yrJW_zsMUXM @ 00:01:53].

Two more consensus points separate pros from victims. First, an NCNDA is a shield, not a paycheck: Trade Base Hub states flatly that NCNDAs do not define payment, commissions, or services, and using one as a substitute for a compensation agreement is a common and costly mistake [yrJW_zsMUXM @ 00:01:36]. IXH agrees, saying the intermediary's commission is often secured by a separate fee protection agreement and must be put in writing with amount, currency, timing, and payment route [5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:08:10]. Second, the fake ICC paperwork circulating online is a scam signal. Cangem Global says there is no such thing as an ICC irrevocable master fee protection agreement, that 100% of IMFPAs and 99% of NCNDAs you will encounter are fake, and that any document citing ICC 400, 500, or 600 belongs in the garbage bin [HldBP9R47Bg @ 00:00:24]. Brufokes African Foods Export recorded their own screen while buying the authentic copy, confirmed the fake version carries phony references to ICC regulations 400, 500, and 600, and said such a document will not be enforced by the ICC [suL1t0XynNw @ 00:00:42]. The genuine document is ICC publication 769, the model occasional intermediary contract, sold through the ICC business bookstore and national committees.

sections.heading: Section 2: Exact Street Mechanics, Tools & Numbers
paragraphs: The ICC model is the commodity desk's gold standard, and Cangem Global walks its mechanics line by line. It is ICC publication 769E, a 27-page e-copy bought directly from the ICC website; purchasers can reuse it for any number of deals but cannot redistribute or resell it [HldBP9R47Bg @ 00:04:58]. The fillable special conditions start around page 15 or 16, and the structure is rigid: one intermediary, who receives commission, and one counterpart, who pays it. You cannot stack sellers and buyers in one column, and Cangem warns that taking commission from both sides gets complicated and can fall into conflict of interest, so pick one payer [HldBP9R47Bg @ 00:06:53]. UpCounsel describes the same split as Part A special conditions completed by each party and Part B standard ICC clauses, with intermediary roles running from passive introductions to active negotiation support and performance monitoring [B7w7HuoPnsA @ 00:00:38]. IXH notes an updated edition of the ICC model was published in 2024 and that it covers intermediary services, remuneration, confidentiality, the undertaking not to compete, term, and applicable law and dispute resolution [5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:03:19]. Remuneration options inside the form include a lump sum, a percentage, or case-by-case pricing, since one document can cover many deals rather than a single transaction.

On the real-estate and business-brokerage side, the mechanics are about speed and leverage. Ron Rohde, on Adventures in CRE, says roughly 99% of listing-broker confidentiality agreements are now electronic signature documents that automatically grant data-room access, and recommends auto-populating the prospect's name straight from CRM entries [EL2eIKZ_OV8 @ 00:01:01]. He wants the property identified precisely even across multiple parcels and outparcels, a carve-out for public information, use limited solely to the purchase, and separate forms for direct principals versus brokers receiving information for a client. His arbitration logic is tactical: as the plaintiff holding the data you want arbitration because it is cheaper and faster; on the defense side you avoid it, since a single arbitrator makes it very high risk [EL2eIKZ_OV8 @ 00:03:33]. David C Barnett flips the script for buyers facing broker NDAs that demand financials. If a deal needs $100,000 down and you hold $500,000, move $100,000 into a separate account, write '$100,000 plus' on the net worth statement, and show a redacted statement over Zoom [wHxYmcrcq4M @ 00:04:06]. He also tells buyers to hand the broker their own NDA protecting buyer information; brokers can refuse, but it signals sophistication [wHxYmcrcq4M @ 00:05:43].

The clause stack that holds up is consistent and numeric. Santiago Cueto lists four essentials: an iron-clad non-circumvention clause covering existing and potential contacts, a confidentiality clause, a liquidated damages clause that pre-sets the financial penalty so enforcement is predictable and costly litigation is minimized, and a duration-and-remedies clause naming injunctive relief or actual damages [6G7yTaLd04k @ 00:01:11]. On numbers, iTopixs treats two years from disclosure as reasonable, has seen one, two, and five, and says courts may strike or revise anything drifting toward five years or more as an unreasonable restraint; the same template adds a two-year non-solicitation of staff, a reasonable-care floor, need-to-know access, and return-or-destroy backed by a sworn statement covering electronic copies [l9rVUJ2duT8 @ 00:16:17]. Cangem puts the street ceiling lower: one to three years, with three already 'a hard bet' and anything beyond it 'daydreaming' [HldBP9R47Bg @ 00:09:23]. Clausehound adds that non-compete and non-solicit terms are not core to every NDA and are often too preliminary for early talks, but where client lists or sales leads change hands, a non-circumvent stops the recipient exploiting those leads, and these covenants usually survive termination [HN8Y7XiYRGE @ 00:01:56].

callout.title: What the desks actually do before paper changes hands
callout.body: Small drafting and sourcing moves separate a protected introduction from a burned one.
items: Treat any NCNDA quoting ICC 400, 500, or 600 regulations as a scam signal and refuse to sign it; the ICC itself says those rules do not exist [IXH TRADING Academy — 5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:04:01]

On the ICC 769 special conditions, leave applicable law blank so the law where the document is signed governs, then choose between ICC arbitration and local courts in the dispute box [Cangem Global Corporation — HldBP9R47Bg @ 00:10:06]

As a buyer, cross out any broker NDA language making you liable for the broker's commission; the buyer is not a party to the seller-broker commission agreement [David C Barnett Small Business and Deal Making SMB — wHxYmcrcq4M @ 00:07:36]
Read every NDA for buried non-competes; Rafael Ludwig sent documents back that barred two years of similar work defined as broadly as video production [Rafael Ludwig — WjchmVIKv5M @ 00:02:08]

sop_steps.title: Verify identity, authority, and capacity
sop_steps.action: Collect a client information sheet or KYC pack, government photo ID, and proof of signing authority from every party.
sop_steps.detail: Courts do not enforce agreements where the parties cannot be clearly identified, and the counterparty's company registration, bank references, and compliance checks should be verified while staying wary of advance-fee requests [Trade Base Hub — yrJW_zsMUXM @ 00:00:33] [IXH TRADING Academy — 5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:07:49]

sop_steps.title: Source genuine paper
sop_steps.action: Buy ICC publication 769E directly from the ICC for intermediary deals, or use a lawyer-drafted NDA for simple confidentiality.
sop_steps.detail: Any ICC-branded NCNDA or IMFPA pulled from a free online template search is most likely fake; the 27-page ICC e-copy can be reused across your own deals but not shared [Cangem Global Corporation — HldBP9R47Bg @ 00:11:45]

sop_steps.title: Define scope, fee route, and term
sop_steps.action: Name the specific opportunity or attach a scope annexure, put the commission in a separate fee agreement, and set a reasonable term.
sop_steps.detail: Vague scope is one of the most common failure reasons, while fees need amount, currency, timing, and payment route spelled out in writing [Trade Base Hub — yrJW_zsMUXM @ 00:00:50] [IXH TRADING Academy — 5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:08:10]

sop_steps.title: Execute before disclosure and keep the evidence trail
sop_steps.action: Get signatures before sharing anything protected, store records, and on breach document evidence and send written notice.
sop_steps.detail: Execution must precede disclosure and be stored with proper records; e-sign platforms log IP, email, and timestamps, and on breach you document evidence, send written notice, and follow the dispute clause [Trade Base Hub — yrJW_zsMUXM @ 00:01:53] [IXH TRADING Academy — 5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:09:08]

sections.heading: Section 3: Where Practitioners Disagree & Alternative Playbooks
paragraphs: The sharpest split is whether only one paper counts. Cangem Global Corporation takes the hard line: 100% of documents calling themselves an IMFPA are fake, 99% of documents circulating as NCNDAs are fake, and the only genuine ICC version is ICC publication 769E, the occasional intermediary non-circumvention non-disclosure model sold on the ICC website [HldBP9R47Bg @ 00:00:24]. Cangem still grades a non-ICC NCNDA as an okay document you can work with, but warns there will be no ICC or third-party arbitration behind it and a lot of limitations [HldBP9R47Bg @ 00:03:38]. Trade Base Hub runs the opposite playbook: properly structured NCNDAs are enforceable both domestically and internationally because courts focus on clarity, identification, scope, and substance, not geography, and poor drafting fails everywhere [yrJW_zsMUXM @ 00:02:09]. iTopixs Videos sits in the working middle, walking through a three-page, three-party NCND on Russian export blend crude that sends disputes to arbitration in the District of Columbia, lets a court of competent jurisdiction enforce the award, and picks a body of international contract principles instead of any national law [l9rVUJ2duT8 @ 00:19:05]. IXH TRADING Academy bridges both camps: many parties start from the ICC model, but whether the agreement holds up depends on the drafting and on the governing law, not on the logo at the top of the page [5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:05:03].

Term length is where the numbers diverge most. Cangem Global Corporation tells intermediaries to fill the ICC term field at one, two, or three years, says even three years is a hard bet with a counterpart, and calls anything beyond that daydreaming [HldBP9R47Bg @ 00:09:43]. IXH TRADING Academy publishes a wider band, commonly two to five years and longer in some sectors, as long as the duration stays reasonable and clearly stated [5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:02:58]. iTopixs Videos anchors on two years for both the confidentiality tail and the non-circumvention window, notes that some parties push for ten, and warns that once a restriction reaches the five-year range courts may call it an unreasonable business restraint and strike the clause or revise it to a shorter period [l9rVUJ2duT8 @ 00:15:59]. John Ferrell, Esq. comes at it from the signer's side: months, a year, or perhaps three years is reasonable, but long contracts get lost, people change positions, and contractual integrity is hard to maintain, so anything spanning multiple years should be questioned on how it will actually be managed [4L_UjIQJoNA @ 00:08:02]. The working read for an introducer: two years is the only number that sits inside every one of these ranges, while anything past three draws resistance from Cangem and Ferrell and a judicial haircut risk from iTopixs.

Whether money belongs inside the NCNDA splits the room. IXH TRADING Academy builds fees into the core: the non-circumvention clause bars closing with introduced parties without written consent and fee sharing, and commission is secured as its own building block, often backed by a separate fee protection agreement [5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:02:39]. Trade Base Hub draws a hard line the other way: NCNDAs are protective instruments, not commercial agreements, they do not define payment, commissions, or services, and using one as a substitute is a common and costly mistake [yrJW_zsMUXM @ 00:01:36]. Cangem Global Corporation adds a structural rule from the ICC 769E special conditions: one intermediary, one counterpart, and commission from either the seller or the buyer, never both, because taking it from both sides gets complicated and can fall into conflict of interest [HldBP9R47Bg @ 00:07:09]. On the buy side, David C Barnett Small Business and Deal Making SMB flips the question entirely, recounting a California Association of Business Brokers standard NDA that made a breaching buyer liable for the broker's commission and telling buyers to cross that language out, because the commission sits strictly between seller and broker [wHxYmcrcq4M @ 00:07:16]. Barnett's posture rests on leverage: a buyer's only leverage is willingness to walk, and a broker who refuses to strike the clause is likely sitting on a listing too crowded to produce a good deal anyway [wHxYmcrcq4M @ 00:08:27].

sections.heading: Section 4: Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: The most expensive failure the speakers describe is an introduction with nothing on paper. IXH TRADING Academy walks through a broker in Alexandria who introduces a grain supplier to a West African importer with nothing signed; the two trade directly and the broker hears about it later with no proof of the role, the fee, or the confidentiality of the contacts [5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:07:09]. Attorney Nancy Greene exposes the second trap: a plain NDA has a huge loophole, because a counterpart who tells no one and simply uses your opportunity has probably not breached it; in Greene's example a mover takes a relocation package to market without the originator, which only a good non-circumvention provision would catch [FOUV15TeRLY @ 00:00:42]. The Altierior Motive with Dr. Chad Michael Altieri warns that even a signed clause fails when it matters most if it is vague, too narrow, too broad, or missing key parties, then lists the audit questions, including whether it covers affiliates and related parties, how long protection survives, and what remedy applies [sm21N5L0nl8 @ 00:01:00]. Trade Base Hub closes the timing gap: the NCNDA must be executed by authorized parties before any protected information is shared, stored with proper records, and poor execution undermines enforceability [yrJW_zsMUXM @ 00:01:53].

The second trap is counterfeit paper. Cangem Global Corporation shows an elaborate NCNDA and IMFPA carrying an ICC logo and references to ICC 400, 500, and 600, says no such regulations exist, and tells operators that if this document ever lands in front of them they should not sign it and should throw it in the garbage bin [HldBP9R47Bg @ 00:01:10]. Brufokes African Foods Export Ltd traced the same problem through an article linking to the ICC's own warning, states that any NCNDA quoting regulations 400, 500, 600 is fake and will not be enforced by the ICC, then recorded the purchase of the genuine publication 769 from the ICC business bookstore [suL1t0XynNw @ 00:00:42]. Going genuine carries its own constraint: Brufokes cannot share the purchased document except with trade partners for the intention of trade [suL1t0XynNw @ 00:01:23], and Cangem reads the ICC copyright as unlimited use by the purchaser across any deals but no redistribution or resale [HldBP9R47Bg @ 00:04:58]. IXH TRADING Academy ties fake paper to fraud, flagging requests for advance fees to issue guarantees or documents as a pattern the ICC's commercial crime services have warned about for years, and telling operators to verify company registration, bank references, and compliance checks before trusting anyone [5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:08:10].

Signers get burned too. Rafael Ludwig received NDAs with non-compete language buried inside, sent at least a couple back because one barred them from working for two years on anything similar, as generic as video production, and signed others that warned of social-media monitoring and heavy, heavy penalties [WjchmVIKv5M @ 00:01:54]. The deals Ludwig did sign left a three-and-a-half-year hole in the reel, forcing a rebuild of client relationships and personal projects just to prove capability [WjchmVIKv5M @ 00:03:30]. David C Barnett Small Business and Deal Making SMB flags the reverse leak: broker NDAs protect the seller's information, not the buyer's, so a buyer holding $500,000 who needs a $100,000 down payment should move $100,000 into a separate account, show only that statement, write $100,000 plus on the net worth form [wHxYmcrcq4M @ 00:04:06], and ask the broker to sign the buyer's own NDA [wHxYmcrcq4M @ 00:05:43]. John Ferrell, Esq. adds that overly broad NDAs discourage collaboration, create confusion, and breed disputes over what was agreed [4L_UjIQJoNA @ 00:06:31], and that insisting on NDAs for readily available public information reduces the credibility of the insisting party [4L_UjIQJoNA @ 00:07:08]. Adventures in CRE confirms that the public-information exclusion is the most common defense a recipient raises [EL2eIKZ_OV8 @ 00:02:16].

callout.title: Four Kill Switches Before Any Introduction Leaves Your Hands
callout.body: Every one of these gates comes from a loss, a fake document, or a burned signer the practitioners reported firsthand. Fail any gate and the introduction stays in your pocket.
items: Kill any document citing ICC 400, 500, or 600 regulations or calling itself an ICC IMFPA; it is fake and belongs in the garbage bin [Cangem Global Corporation — HldBP9R47Bg @ 00:01:10].

Share zero protected names, prices, or shipping data until authorized signatories have executed the NCNDA and completed a client information sheet or KYC with government photo ID [Trade Base Hub — yrJW_zsMUXM @ 00:00:33].

Confirm the paper is a real non-circumvention instrument, not a plain NDA, and that it covers affiliates and related parties, survival period, and remedy [The Altierior Motive with Dr. Chad Michael Altieri — sm21N5L0nl8 @ 00:01:15].
Walk away from any counterparty requesting advance fees to issue guarantees or documents, and verify registration and bank references first [IXH TRADING Academy — 5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:08:10].

chapters.pull_quote: Where an NDA is a don't tell anyone about my stuff clause, a non-circumvention provision is a don't do my stuff without me clause. — Attorney Nancy Greene (FOUV15TeRLY @ 00:01:00).
action_checklist: Buy the genuine ICC publication 769E ecopy directly from the ICC website, fill only the special conditions, and keep the 27-page general conditions intact [Cangem Global Corporation — HldBP9R47Bg @ 00:11:22].
Collect a client information sheet or KYC package with valid government-issued photo ID from every party before the NCNDA is signed [Trade Base Hub — yrJW_zsMUXM @ 00:00:33].
Define the specific opportunity or list scopes in a formal annexure that is updated and executed by all parties [Trade Base Hub — yrJW_zsMUXM @ 00:01:05].

Add a liquidated damages clause with a pre-agreed financial penalty for circumventing contacts or disclosing confidential information [Santiago Cueto | Miami Business Litigation Lawyer — 6G7yTaLd04k @ 00:01:11].

Execute through DocuSign or Adobe Sign so IP addresses, emails, and timestamps prove who signed and when, reserving notarization for highly sensitive trade secrets [County Portal Law — FKep5tuU15Q @ 00:01:38].
On breach, document the evidence, send written notice, follow the dispute clause, and use urgent court measures to stop further harm [IXH TRADING Academy — 5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:09:08].

chapters.question_prompt: How do practitioners enter yacht and aircraft brokerage, source vessels, work with luxury clients, and evaluate sales and charter economics?
chapters.title: Yacht and Aircraft Brokerage: Entry, Sourcing, and Economics
chapters.subtitle: Aircraft brokerage startup, yacht-broker compensation, luxury-client service, yacht sourcing, operator-document checks, charter investment economics, and broker-panel case studies
chapters.executive_summary: Yacht and aircraft brokers agree the trade runs on trust, referrals, and relationships, not credentials: aircraft sales carry no FAA license and no training path, while only Florida and California license yacht brokers. Entry means living in a yacht hub, taking any yachting job, and farming captains and managers for leads. On yachts, the street schedule pays 10% on the first $10M, 5% on the next $10M, and 2.5% per $10M after, split 60/40 toward the buyer's broker; a junior on a 20% house split nets $80K off a $1M commission. Aircraft commissions slide from about 10% on $50K planes to 0.5-1% on a $40M G550. Practitioners clash on whether 10% is fixed or negotiable, on going solo versus joining a big house, and on chasing mega-deals versus building volume pipelines.

sections.title: The Practitioner Consensus
paragraphs: Every practitioner on this beat lands on the same foundation: the deal moves on trust, and trust compounds into referrals. Gerry Mendria calls integrity the key and says the business is strictly referral and repeat, warning that anyone whose main motive is commission would fit better in another business [5hRyQr7CMkA @ 00:00:17]. The Yacht Broker Masterclass instructor reduces it to one line, saying it really is a relationships business, and backs that up with a broker who visited an owner at home and surfaced a 70m build [_Shd1I2mefI @ 00:13:10]. Wealth Pilot puts the same point in buyer terms: clients buy from people they trust and know, and the recurring money that follows a closed deal comes from management and charter commissions plus a resale roughly five years later [WWrDBEGo6gM @ 00:03:24]. On the aircraft side, GLADA chairman Phil Jordan stresses that aircraft sales has no training path and no regulation, which is why the association built an online course of 8 to 9 sections with quizzes and a certificate, plus an internal channel for planes not yet on the market and pre-buy openings [i36Xg_tsVAY @ 00:02:56]. Jordan's sharpest line on the gap: a haircut legally requires a license, while selling a multimillion-dollar jet does not, so reputation becomes the only credential a buyer can actually check.

The entry path is consistent across yacht and aircraft practitioners: get physically close to the asset and its owners before trying to sell it. The Yacht Broker Masterclass sets the first step as moving to a yacht hub such as Fort Lauderdale, Palma, or Antibes, taking any yachting-associated job even if no brokerage company hires you immediately, and networking with captains and yacht managers who become future lead sources [-7bW4uN98Hc @ 00:00:23]. David, a Northrop & Johnson broker formerly at Camper & Nicholsons, confirms what the houses actually screen for: connections, yacht knowledge, networking ability, and a sales record, with a degree nowhere on the list [FpmvbD9-7yc @ 00:03:08]. Gerry Mendria adds that boating experience was only a partial advantage, which fits the pattern of relationships outranking seamanship [5hRyQr7CMkA @ 00:00:46]. Aircraft entry is even lighter. Alex Bengoechea states that no FAA license is needed to broker aircraft, including at someone else's brokerage; some states require an aircraft dealer license that works like a business license with no test, Arizona and Washington add a surety bond, Florida only requires Department of Revenue registration, and the build-out is an LLC plus an EIN [p6XXGAWrnB8 @ 00:00:14]. The shared baseline is access, product fluency, and patience while the network matures into buyer and seller leads.

Nobody pretends the income is steady. Wealth Pilot states flatly that brokers do not earn a steady salary, pay for Monaco, Miami, and Fort Lauderdale boat shows out of pocket, earn $0 when a deal falls through, and can run 18 months with no deal before an 8-figure payday lands, calling it a feast or famine economy [WWrDBEGo6gM @ 00:01:07]. Gerry Mendria lived the seasonal version: working every single day from May until after Labor Day with no time for family or boating, then a winter that went dead, meaning no income coming in at all [5hRyQr7CMkA @ 00:02:44]. Tomic of W Yachts frames the cure as volume rather than whale hunting: ten $100k sales or twenty $50k sales can equal one $1M sale, and brokers who only chase the big fish fall into a feast-or-famine cycle that ends in burnout, because consistency trumps singularity [elBm9ZOqdsA @ 00:02:22]. David reaches the same verdict from inside a major house, calling yacht sales a high-risk, high-reward industry where the headline commission gets carved up long before it reaches a junior broker's account [FpmvbD9-7yc @ 00:15:06]. The working prerequisite every one of these operators implies is a cash cushion sized for long dry stretches and a pipeline deep enough that one collapsed deal does not end the year.

sections.title: Exact Street Mechanics, Tools & Numbers
paragraphs: The yacht commission schedule the house-trained brokers quote is tiered: 10% on the first $10M, 5% on the next $10M, and 2.5% on each $10M after that, so a $30M yacht carries a potential $1.75M commission [FpmvbD9-7yc @ 00:05:18]. The Yacht Broker Masterclass instructor runs the same ladder on a $100M yacht: $1M on the first $10M, $500,000 on the second, then $250,000 per additional $10M [_Shd1I2mefI @ 00:05:41]. That commission is then split 60% to the buyer's broker and 40% to the seller's broker, so on a $1M commission a broker on a 50/50 house split keeps $300,000 representing the buyer or $200,000 representing the seller [_Shd1I2mefI @ 00:07:06]. David's worked example shows how fast the gross shrinks in practice. A yacht asking $30M sells at $25M for a $1.625M commission, but the seller insists on $24M net, which drops the commission to $1M. David defends the 60/40 tilt bluntly, since the buyer's broker can always steer the client to another yacht. After the co-broker takes that share, the house keeps $400,000; a junior broker on 20% walks away with $80,000, while a senior broker on a 50/50 split with no wage clears about $200,000 from the same sale [FpmvbD9-7yc @ 00:13:22]. The lesson in the arithmetic: the headline percentage is never the check.

Pay structure is where new brokers get burned or protected. The Yacht Broker Masterclass instructor lays out the menu: apprentices may get a small basic wage with a lower split, trainee splits run 30/70 or 20/80, the instructor's own first employer paid 20%, and independent contractors get 50/50 but fund their own flights and hotels, the example being trips to the Exumas. The trap is the clawback, where 2,000 to 3,000 a month in pay is treated as an advance against commission and recovered out of the first sale, so it has to be clarified before signing [_Shd1I2mefI @ 00:03:06]. New builds pay differently: Lurssen and Amels deals usually pay about 5% rather than 10%, and Benetti ratchets the fee from introduction only, to introduction plus contract, to full commission for brokers who make regular shipyard visits [_Shd1I2mefI @ 00:11:20]. David pegs junior house packages at a small wage plus roughly 10 to 20% of the house commission, with office space, cards, boat-show access, and a shared assistant, and notes that a higher wage always means a lower percentage [FpmvbD9-7yc @ 00:07:30]. Charter runs in its own lane: Behind the Gold reports charter brokers earn up to 20%, on superyachts whose running costs sit around 10% of value per year, so a EUR 100M yacht burns roughly EUR 10M annually [LBp3Cz4zFQI @ 00:01:22].

Aircraft brokerage runs on a tighter cost stack and a sliding fee. Alex Bengoechea prices the toolkit line by line: JetNet at $750 a month on a 12-month contract, Controller ads at $600 to $2,000, and a photographer at $1,500 to $2,000 or about $500 for a budget shooter, with the rule to buy subscriptions only when a deal needs them and to start in piston aircraft, which are easier to enter than jets that demand cash reserves [p6XXGAWrnB8 @ 00:04:13]. Commission slides with price: about 10% on a roughly $50,000 aircraft, about 6% on a $500,000 Navajo or a $1M aircraft, and 1% or 0.5% on a $40M G550, and Bengoechea always pushes for an exclusive over a non-exclusive agreement [p6XXGAWrnB8 @ 00:17:26]. Phil Jordan's GLADA playbook front-loads the deal team: an aviation tax adviser, finance, an escrow agent and escrow agreement, and a broker contract, plus a deposit or retainer on acquisitions and some sales so the broker is not working for free [i36Xg_tsVAY @ 00:18:24]. Jordan also warns that a general CPA lacks aviation tax knowledge; the host cited a $17,000 tax bill from a state the owner does not even live in, and when a client pushes back, the fix is having the client's own accountant call the aviation specialist directly [i36Xg_tsVAY @ 00:21:44].

callout.title: Street Moves That Protect the Commission
callout.body: Four moves working brokers use to keep deals inside their own hands and close before the asset goes stale.
items: Keep the seller off the yacht during showings; David flags the cut-out risk when owner and buyer meet directly [Yachts For Sale — FpmvbD9-7yc @ 00:33:11].
Visit owners at home: one broker learned of a 70m build that way, and a 70m sale can bring about $1M even after the house split [Yacht Broker Masterclass — _Shd1I2mefI @ 00:14:59].
Move on off-market aircraft early and treat the first offer as one of the best before the listing becomes a stinky fish and a desperation sale [Own The Jet — i36Xg_tsVAY @ 00:15:19].
Before booking a charter, demand the operator's AOC and D085, insurance, company and registration numbers, and hull number [International Aircraft Broker Institute IABI — xl7JC2nh0UQ @ 00:00:00].

sop_steps.title: Plant Yourself in a Yacht Hub
sop_steps.action: Relocate to Fort Lauderdale, Palma, or Antibes and take any yachting-associated job.
sop_steps.detail: Brokerage work may not come immediately, but a yachting job puts you next to captains and yacht managers who later feed buyer and seller leads [Yacht Broker Masterclass — -7bW4uN98Hc @ 00:00:45].

sop_steps.title: Negotiate the Pay Structure Up Front
sop_steps.action: Choose between a wage and a higher split, and pin down any clawback before signing.
sop_steps.detail: Gerry Mendria refused any wage in exchange for a higher commission percentage and hit a two-year profitability target in 6 months [Gerry Mendria — 5hRyQr7CMkA @ 00:01:32]; clarify whether 2,000 to 3,000 a month is an advance recovered from the first sale [Yacht Broker Masterclass — _Shd1I2mefI @ 00:03:06].

sop_steps.title: Screen Every Buyer Before Showing
sop_steps.action: Run Google searches, collect proof of funds, and complete KYC and AML checks.
sop_steps.detail: David screens buyers with Google, proof of funds, KYC, and AML, then checks names on World-Check before access to the yacht [Yachts For Sale — FpmvbD9-7yc @ 00:28:46].

sop_steps.title: Close Through Escrow and Binding Paper
sop_steps.action: Move from non-binding LOI to binding APA with a lawyer on retainer, and close through escrow.
sop_steps.detail: Bengoechea always uses escrow via AIC Title or Aerospace Reports, usually splitting the fee, and says there is a way without escrow but does not recommend it [Alex Bengoechea — p6XXGAWrnB8 @ 00:21:23].

sections.title: Where Practitioners Disagree & Alternative Playbooks
paragraphs: The sharpest fault line is whether the 10% headline is law or opening bid. David of Yachts For Sale, a Northrop & Johnson broker, works the classic tiered schedule as standard: 10% on the first $10M, 5% on the second $10M, 2.5% per $10M after that, so a $30M yacht carries a potential $1.75M commission [FpmvbD9-7yc @ 00:05:18]. Yacht Broker Masterclass runs the same ladder and the same 60/40 split favoring the buyer's broker, while admitting brokers often need flexibility on commission [_Shd1I2mefI @ 00:05:17]. Current Yachts attacks the premise head-on. Amanda Haley and Maryline Bossar say the 10% is mostly un-negotiated, that it sometimes gets negotiated to 8%, and that fixed commissions risk being price setting; their stance is blunt: it is not set at 10% [wqPY1eV4vuQ @ 00:21:38]. They let the seller choose whether to co-broke at all, recommending at least 4% compensation but allowing two, three, four or eight. On the aircraft side Alex Bengoechea treats the percentage as a sliding function of ticket size: about 10% on a $50K airplane, roughly 6% on a $500K Navajo or $1M aircraft, and 1% or 0.5% on a $40M G550 [p6XXGAWrnB8 @ 00:17:26]. Operator takeaway: quote the schedule, but know which camp your counterparty sits in before you defend it.

Pay structure splits practitioners into two camps. Gerry Mendria refused any wage outright in exchange for a higher percentage of the commission, called it win-win, took over and renovated an office facing a competitor, and turned a two-year profitability projection into six months [5hRyQr7CMkA @ 00:01:32]. Yacht Broker Masterclass maps the safer path: apprentices take a small basic wage at a lower split, trainees run 30/70 or 20/80, and the speaker's own first employer kept 80 while they got 20; independent contractors jump to 50/50 but fund their own flights and hotels down to the Exumas [_Shd1I2mefI @ 00:04:37]. David at Yachts For Sale prices the same trade-off from the junior seat: a small wage plus about 10 to 20% of house commission, office space, cards, boat-show access and a shared assistant, with the rule that a higher wage means a lower percentage. On going solo, David draws a hard line: it works if you hold a buyer network, but seller-side brokers need a large house for credibility, websites, legal support and show access [FpmvbD9-7yc @ 00:16:31]. Current Yachts sidesteps the debate entirely, shifting from a commission-based to a service-based model with a $1,500 listing prep and promotion fee [wqPY1eV4vuQ @ 00:30:02].

Entry and sourcing playbooks diverge just as hard. Yacht Broker Masterclass insists you physically relocate to Fort Lauderdale, Palma or Antibes, take any yachting-associated job, and network with captains and yacht managers until buyer and seller leads surface through patience and tenacity [-7bW4uN98Hc @ 00:00:23]. Alex Bengoechea runs aircraft prospecting from a desk: the public FAA owner database, skip tracing, cold calls and postcards, plus Facebook Marketplace, which they say works less well now [p6XXGAWrnB8 @ 00:16:17]. Ali Merchant on the IABI podcast says no standard sourcing software exists for charter; they built a private roster of 2,500+ operators spanning owners, central agents and captain-managers covering 40 to 400 ft yachts [Oxw138mRpnA @ 00:07:39]. Europe demands 3-day minimums while the US caps charters at 13 guests. Deal-size strategy splits too. Tomic of W Yachts argues consistency trumps singularity: 10 sales at $100k or 20 at $50k can match one $1M sale, and chasing only the big fish breeds a feast-or-famine cycle and burnout [elBm9ZOqdsA @ 00:02:22]. On a 5% kept commission, €20M in volume equals €1M, reachable as 2 x €10M, 4 x €5M, 10 x €2M or 20 x €1M. Pick the playbook that matches your geography, capital reserves, network depth and tolerance for long dry months between closes.

sections.title: Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: The most-reported trap is cash flow. Gerry Mendria worked every single day from May until after Labor Day with no time for family or boating, then watched winter go dead, meaning no income coming in, which pushed them into an online business for residual income [5hRyQr7CMkA @ 00:02:44]. Wealth Pilot puts the same risk in plain numbers: brokers do not earn a steady salary, boat shows in Monaco, Miami and Fort Lauderdale come out of pocket, pay is $0 when a deal falls through, and a broker can go 18 months with no deal before an 8-figure close, which they call a feast or famine economy [WWrDBEGo6gM @ 00:02:09]. David at Yachts For Sale confesses the classic rookie blowout: after a first big sale, a top-100 yacht under NDA, they overspent on a car and hotels; the fix is to treat every commission as your last [FpmvbD9-7yc @ 00:23:00]. Yacht Broker Masterclass flags the hidden version of the same problem: a clawback where 2 to 3,000 a month in pay is really an advance against commission, recovered from your first sale, so clarify it before signing [_Shd1I2mefI @ 00:03:06]. Budget for dead winter months and failed deals before you budget for the next yacht show.

Overpricing is the second killer. David pitched a Monaco owner against five brokers, advising an ask of 30, serious attention to offers over 25, and an expected landing near 27; rivals promised 35 and a 33 sale, won the listing, and the yacht sat two years, was cut to 27, and sold for less [FpmvbD9-7yc @ 00:25:05]. Phil Jordan of GLADA reaches the same verdict from aircraft: the first offer is one of your best, and a listing that sits becomes a stinky fish that ends in a desperation sale [i36Xg_tsVAY @ 00:15:59]. Current Yachts lists the seller-side errors behind stale inventory: emotional pricing, upgrades that never return their cost, and holding costs like insurance, hull cleaning and washing while boats take four to six months to sell once listed [wqPY1eV4vuQ @ 00:27:05]. They also catch listing misrepresentation in the wild: a spec saying Volvo when the engine was a Yanmar, and Garmin units swapped for Raymarine. Jordan's own red flags for aircraft are a spec sheet with no registration or serial number and a middleman markup, illustrated as $650 versus $750. David's market rule closes it out: a boat a year on market and still unsold means the market is telling you something.

Deal mechanics fail where controls are skipped. Current Yachts reports about one in ten deals reject after survey; a $25K generator problem found at survey ends in an allowance, an escrow holdback or rejection, so the 10% deposit goes into trust before anything else [wqPY1eV4vuQ @ 00:55:01]. David keeps the seller off the yacht during showings because of cut-out risk, screens buyers through Google, proof of funds, KYC, AML and World-Check, and insists the business relies on cast iron, watertight contracts [FpmvbD9-7yc @ 00:33:11]. The IYBA broker panel shows what happens without them: one broker cut commission 10% for VAT in a side letter while a second badgered the client after contract execution; nobody sues, the business runs on trust, and a Florida tortious interference claim was not pursued because both brokers were in the Med [RPROcS6hZSE @ 00:09:41]. The panel also rules that commission is earned at contract plus deposit, and that an option holds only 48 hours unless a contract and deposit follow. Alex Bengoechea warns the aircraft market is unregulated, says the LOI is non-binding while the APA binds, keeps a lawyer on retainer, and always uses escrow [p6XXGAWrnB8 @ 00:21:23]. Every one of these failures traces back to a missing document, a missing deposit or a missing screening check.

callout.title: Four checks before you sign, list, or wire
callout.body: Every item below maps to a loss, reversal, or bottleneck a named practitioner lived through. Clear all four before committing time or client money.
items: Confirm in writing whether any base pay is a clawback advance recovered from your first sale before accepting a brokerage seat [Yacht Broker Masterclass — _Shd1I2mefI @ 00:03:06].
Refuse to win a listing on a fantasy number: ask 30 to land near 27 rather than promise 35 and watch the yacht sit two years [Yachts For Sale — FpmvbD9-7yc @ 00:25:05].
Run every closing through escrow; there is a way to do it without escrow, and the practitioner does not recommend it [Alex Bengoechea — p6XXGAWrnB8 @ 00:21:23].
Assemble the aviation tax adviser, finance, escrow agent, escrow agreement and broker contract up front, and take a deposit or retainer on acquisitions [Own The Jet — i36Xg_tsVAY @ 00:18:24].

chapters.question_prompt: How do I explain and protect my commission, address buyer-agent compensation, and handle disbursement and closing wires without overlooking fraud risks?
chapters.title: Protecting Commissions and Collecting at Closing
chapters.subtitle: Aircraft and yacht fees, jet-broker commission agreements and markups, circumvention risks, buyer-broker agreements, seller-paid compensation disputes, escrow instructions, and wire-fraud prevention
chapters.executive_summary: Jet, yacht, commodity and real estate closers agree on one rule: lock the fee in writing before the deal gets exposed. That means a listing, an off-market exclusive, a one-page commission agreement naming the buyer, or a non-circumvention clause. Then strip tail and serial numbers so nobody can go around you, and treat closing-day wires as the main point of loss. The numbers are blunt. Aircraft fees run 1% to 10%. A 10% yacht commission nets the working broker about 2.5% after splits. Charter margins swing from 5% to 30% per trip, and a clean disbursement form pays in 24 hours. The disagreements center on the spread. Jet brokers teach net-price and intermediary resale structures, while MarginCallMedia calls the undisclosed markup a conflict that drains clients and squeezes operators. Residential agents instead fund buyer-paid fees through rate credits and seller concessions.

sections.heading: Section 1: The Practitioner Consensus
paragraphs: Every closer in this group starts from the same rule: no signature, no specs. The Ultimate Jet Guide host says the single most important thing is having something in writing that spells out how you get paid before you start sending specs. When two end users deal through you, you need a signed piece of paper from at least one of them committing to your fee [1ILeO7AapJM @ 00:05:44]. Sam Cutting runs the commodity version of the same play. Source the seller and get a commission or partnership agreement giving you permission to sell and promote. If you hold the buyer, get the buyer to sign a commission agreement instead. The broker who actually connects buyer and seller collects far more often than the broker who introduced a broker to a broker [QguZjBADFoA @ 00:01:04]. The Pryderi Podcast treats the paper as protection for a real asset. Introductions to family offices, billionaires and ready buyers take months or years to build, and a non-circumvention clause makes going around the middleman a contractual violation exposed to damages [rnUvOWiFpDQ @ 00:01:35]. Cutting adds a hard filter on top of the paperwork. When an NCNDA lands with 14 intermediaries attached, that deal is never going to close, so get out of any chain with more than two entities [QguZjBADFoA @ 00:00:22].

The second point of agreement is that commission is a percentage of price, so asset size drives the check more than the rate does. Alex Bengoechea quotes aircraft brokers at 1% to 10% and walks the math. A 2006 Hawker 850 XB at $5 million and 1.5% pays $75,000. A 1978 Cessna 414 at $500,000 and 5% pays $25,000. A 1946 Aranca Champ at $50,000 and 10% pays only $5,000 [Uhqo4raDQ0k @ 00:00:38]. The headline rate also never lands whole. Christopher of Yacht Experts says yacht deals typically carry 10%, split 5% to the buyer's broker and 5% to the seller's broker. The employing licensed broker then takes 50% of each side, so the working broker nets about 2.5% of the sale price [NUVwWnSq3A0 @ 00:01:38]. Yacht Zero describes the same 10% being carved between the listing broker, the person bringing the buyer, and the brokerage houses they are employed by [oEXYo1_yeOU @ 00:00:28]. MarginCallMedia separates the two aviation money streams. Aircraft sales brokers earn a predictable commission paid at closing on low-frequency, high-value deals. Charter brokers take anywhere from 5% to 30% per trip on smaller, frequent bookings [PWGk1rSbFhA @ 00:01:09].

The last consensus point is that the commission is only real once the wire clears, and closing day is where money gets lost. Hauseit calls double- and triple-confirming wire details the single most important takeaway, because an email account at the attorney's firm can be compromised. Call the office, ideally reaching someone you met, read the account and routing numbers aloud, and match them before sending, since a wire fraud victim has little remedy [KrsoinTC_10 @ 00:00:00]. Family Split Strategy explains how the attack works. Hackers get into the weakest inbox on the CC chain, such as a small realtor, inspector or insurer working off home Wi-Fi. They register a look-alike title domain, build a matching website in an hour or two, and email fake wiring instructions [DZe5D7_TCDA @ 00:06:22]. The same speaker applies the defense to brokers directly: a title company should send a test transaction before sending off a commission to a realtor [DZe5D7_TCDA @ 00:12:44]. Lauren of Title's Not Borin' adds the structural constraint. Escrow is a neutral third party that can only act on mutually agreed instruction, and any contract amendment has to reach escrow in writing within three days of acceptance [IK3LgAFr-QQ @ 00:02:05].

sections.heading: Section 2: Exact Street Mechanics, Tools & Numbers
paragraphs: The Ultimate Jet Guide host lays out the off-market capture sequence step by step. If the owner will not sign a normal listing, ask for an exclusive limited to off-market activity for 30, 60 or 90 days, or even a week. In exchange, promise not to publish on Controller, or agree to remove the tail number from everything [1ILeO7AapJM @ 00:00:58]. If the owner only says bring me a buyer, scrub the tail and serial numbers from every photo, including cockpit shots. Avoid sending maintenance reports unless you trust the broker, and send only a spec sheet with times and upgrades. Anyone who can identify the plane can call the seller and say let's not pay the broker [1ILeO7AapJM @ 00:01:38]. Get the seller to agree verbally to a number such as 6% or 4% early. When a buyer bites, send a one-page commission agreement naming that buyer and the amount, payable only if that specific deal goes through. Once it is signed, the floodgates open and the buyer can get anything [1ILeO7AapJM @ 00:03:13]. Alex Bengoechea notes why starting on smaller aircraft is easier. Jets and turboprops demand JetNet or Amstat, professional pictures and Controller ads, none of them cheap, plus a solid track record [Uhqo4raDQ0k @ 00:01:20].

When neither side will pay, the jet playbook shifts to the spread. The Ultimate Jet Guide host first asks the buyer to cover the fee. If the buyer refuses, he asks the seller for a net number, say $2 million, and keeps anything above it [1ILeO7AapJM @ 00:04:13]. The transparent route writes that split into the agreement, but if pre-buy squawks force a $100,000 price cut, the broker earns nothing. The alternative uses an intermediary company that contracts the aircraft at $2 million and offers it to the buyer at $2.1 million with the commission included. The broker pockets the $100,000 difference, and each side chooses whether to proceed [1ILeO7AapJM @ 00:05:04]. MarginCallMedia maps three charter pay models. The operator cut is kicked back out of wholesale profit. The transparent fee appears as separate line items. The undisclosed markup, which it calls the most prevalent method, buys wholesale and resells at whatever the market tolerates, and sub-brokering stacks margin at every hop [PWGk1rSbFhA @ 00:01:42]. Sam Cutting's control play is to take payment yourself: collect from the buyer, pay the seller and keep the exact commission you set. Do this only after full due diligence on the seller, ideally including a face-to-face factory visit [QguZjBADFoA @ 00:01:45].

Splits with outside parties get negotiated down to an exact figure. The Ultimate Jet Guide host asks every broker, pilot or management company early how they are getting paid. When one says whatever you think, he forces a number. If they demand $50,000 out of a $50,000 commission, he counters at $10,000 for just bringing the guy, or $25,000 for getting the deal across the line [1ILeO7AapJM @ 00:07:46]. In residential, Brandon Mulrenin and his lender guest show how to fund a buyer-paid fee on a $460,000 purchase. Raising the rate from 6.125% to 6.625% yields a 1% credit, about $4,300, and lifts the payment from $2,725 to $2,867 [5YNeLidiqqU @ 00:05:44]. The other route writes the price at $473,800 with a $13,800 seller concession. The payment rises only $81, a 170-month or 14-year break-even. The buyer agent fee counts as a customary fee outside the 3% concession limit, but it has to be in the offer before the appraisal is ordered [5YNeLidiqqU @ 00:11:38]. Think Real Estate reports that well over 90% of sellers still agree to pay a buyer broker when asked in the offer. The average buyer's agent commission sits at 2.37%, down from 2.45% [wBbi84Xi1Bc @ 00:01:32].

callout.title: How Closers Keep The Fee Intact From Intro To Disbursement
callout.body: Field-tested moves for anonymizing assets, pinning co-brokers to a number, and getting the commission wire out the door clean.
items: Before any aircraft package goes out, check the cockpit photos for a visible tail number, because that is where it leaks most often [The Ultimate Jet Guide — 1ILeO7AapJM @ 00:01:38]

Never accept 'just whatever you think' from a co-broker. Force an exact figure and counter based on the work done, such as $10,000 for an intro or $25,000 for closing work [The Ultimate Jet Guide — 1ILeO7AapJM @ 00:08:01]

Coach the title attorney or escrow company to list the exact wire amount, their bank's name and their contact information on the disbursement form, so a failed transfer can be traced fast [Equity Real Estate — mVFdzEqW2M4 @ 00:00:51]

Put the concession and buyer agent fee into the offer itself, because the appraiser receives the purchase agreement and adding concessions after the appraisal comes back is too late [Brandon Mulrenin — 5YNeLidiqqU @ 00:13:45]

sop_steps.action: Secure a listing, off-market exclusive, or verbal fee agreement before any identifying details leave your hands.
sop_steps.detail: Ask the owner for a short exclusive limited to off-market activity, then confirm a commission number such as 6% or 4% verbally before pitching any buyer [The Ultimate Jet Guide — 1ILeO7AapJM @ 00:02:49]

sop_steps.action: Send only a scrubbed spec sheet, then convert interest into a signed one-page commission agreement naming the buyer.
sop_steps.detail: Strip tail and serial numbers from photos and reports, and if the buyer's side is the one you control, get the buyer to sign a commission agreement instead [Sam Cutting - Red Flags Verification — QguZjBADFoA @ 00:01:25]

sop_steps.title: Settle Every Split In Writing
sop_steps.action: Ask each outside broker, pilot or management company how they are getting paid, and agree on an exact dollar figure.
sop_steps.detail: Have the conversation early and do not let them control it; split 50/50 only when they are actually doing the work to get the deal across the line [The Ultimate Jet Guide — 1ILeO7AapJM @ 00:06:29]

sop_steps.action: Complete every field on the commission disbursement form and confirm the funding entity's side a day or two before closing.
